Structural Design Tools

Import AutoCAD DXF files or image files in JPEG or PNG format. Import & Analyze converts the detected sheet into editable native grids, members, slabs, footings, frame views, sidebar data, and a 3D view. The raster image is retained only as a review thumbnail.

Required source-drawing format
  • For the standard six-panel sheet use exactly two columns by three rows: FOUNDATION LEVEL / LEVEL-1, LEVEL-2 / LEVEL-3, then X-AXIS FRAME / Y-AXIS FRAME.
  • Use one bordered panel for each drawing and place one centered title below it: FOUNDATION LEVEL, LEVEL-1, LEVEL-2, and so on, X-AXIS FRAME, or Y-AXIS FRAME.
  • Show alphabetic grid bubbles from left to right and numeric grid bubbles from 1 at the top downward; include every individual grid-span dimension.
  • Show each level height on the X-AXIS FRAME or Y-AXIS FRAME, including Foundation-to-Level-1.
  • Use solid lines for structural beams or columns. Dashed/hidden lines are read as no structural member.
  • Use clear square column and footing symbols at grid intersections, and label panels SLAB, SLAB ON-FILL, EARTH-FILLED, or OPEN SPACE.
  • Export PNG whenever possible, at least 3000 px wide. Use solid black, fully opaque text and lines; avoid thin gray JPEG text or compression artifacts.
  • If any detected drawing is inaccurate—not only FOUNDATION—choose its title under Correct one detected drawing, then replace it with a clear crop that retains the title, grid bubbles, dimensions, and complete member extents.
Choose individual titled drawings or one combined drawing sheet. Import & Analyze will separate, validate, and convert it directly into the app's native drawing format.

Plan columns: choose Create Column, then click a plan grid intersection. Create Node can place a junction directly on a girder. In Create Beams mode, click one node and continue through each aligned node. Structural Wall Tool similarly creates continuous slab-supported walls between structural or auxiliary-grid nodes.

Working member dimensions. Change them and recalculate as many times as needed. They apply to all beams or columns except members individually edited in MPR; Economical Design may increase a failing section.

Beginners Tutorials

Start A New Frame

  1. Click Create New Design to clear the drawing area after confirming the warning.
  2. Define the X-grid and Y-grid labels and spans in Structural Plan.
  3. Enter the floor names under Levels and their vertical rises under Level heights.
  4. Click Generate Structural Plan.
  5. Choose Create Column, then click each required plan-grid intersection.
  6. Select the X-frame and Y-frame extraction gridlines to review both elevations.
  7. Choose the active X-axis or Y-axis frame before creating supplemental nodes, members, or supports.
  8. Select the occupancy, materials, wind, and earthquake parameters, then generate the directional loads.
  9. Select a member before assigning a point load or wall line load.
  10. Click Calculate to update reactions, member results, and diagrams.
  11. Use Show/Hide Loading to simplify the drawing view.
  12. Use Print PDF or Print Local for report output.

Load Notes

DL, SDL, LL, WL, and EQL are generated separately. Beam and column self weight remains active in both frame analyses.

Checking Notes

Always review supports, load direction, member sizes, and reaction balance before using results for design documentation.

Important

This tool is for modeling assistance. Final structural calculations must be checked and approved by a licensed Structural or Civil Engineer.
